[UI] Update Font Size � Flutter Migration

QA Tester Summary

Verdict: BUG
Issue: #1 - [UI] Update Font Size
QA Date: 2026-07-27
Build / App Evidence: Android real-device manual video from QA tester
Scope Tested: Typography/font-size system, OpenSans registration, reusable typography scale, hardcoded widget font sizes, and visual behavior on real-device core screens.

Test Scenario Summary

# Method Scenario Evidence Result
1 White Box Verify OpenSans Regular/Bold are registered as Flutter fonts. pubspec.yaml, assets/ font scan Fail
2 White Box Verify app theme uses the requested OpenSans family as the typography source. lib/app/theme.dart, lib/app/typography.dart Fail
3 White Box Verify font sizes come from a single reusable typography scale instead of hardcoded widget values. rg fontSize over lib/ Fail
4 Gray Box Verify central typography helpers exist and are used by many shared components/screens. TourTypography, TourTextContext, component imports Pass
5 Black Box Verify real-device screens are readable at default font settings across login, drawer, tour list, settings, and create-tour flows. Manual Android video Pass
6 Black Box Verify no obvious text clipping/overlap in the recorded core screens. Manual Android video Pass
7 Regression / Accessibility Verify system text scaling behavior against acceptance criteria. Manual video did not clearly isolate Android font-size increase; source review shows no custom blocking of scaling Not fully covered

Code Review Summary

Area Files Reviewed Review Notes Result
Font asset registration pubspec.yaml, assets/ No fonts: section and no OpenSans .ttf/.otf files were found. This fails the OpenSans Regular/Bold acceptance criterion. Fail
Theme typography lib/app/theme.dart Theme uses Typography.geist(...), not OpenSans. The issue explicitly asks OpenSans to be registered and rendered. Fail
Typography scale lib/app/typography.dart A centralized TourTypography scale exists with documented sizes 14/16/18/20/22 and reusable getters. Pass
Hardcoded widget font sizes lib/components/**, lib/features/** Multiple widgets still define direct fontSize values such as 11, 12, 13, and 16 outside the central scale. Fail
Real-device visual readability Manual video Login, navigation drawer, Real Estate list, settings, and create-tour screens are readable and do not show obvious overflow in recorded default-size flow. Pass

Test Type Coverage Result

Black Box Manual real-device recording using real account/data across key app screens. Pass for readability, Fail overall due to source acceptance gaps

Confusion Matrix

Classification Meaning for Issue #1 Observed Count Notes
True Positive A real acceptance failure is correctly detected. 3 Missing OpenSans registration, theme not using OpenSans, hardcoded font sizes remain.
True Negative Expected visual readability passes are correctly detected. 2 Recorded screens are readable and no obvious default-size overflow was observed.
False Positive A failure is reported but acceptance is actually met. 0 Source evidence directly contradicts required OpenSans and single-source criteria.

Test Execution Notes

Command / Evidence Result
`rg -n "OpenSans fontFamily
Get-ChildItem -Recurse assets -File filtered for .ttf/.otf/OpenSans No OpenSans font assets found
rg -n "fontSize:" lib Multiple direct widget fontSize values remain outside the central scale
flutter test test\scene_panorama_card_test.dart test\gothru_screen_test.dart test\scene_settings_sheet_test.dart 2 tests passed, 3 failed; failures are existing/adjacent test harness or expectation issues and not direct proof of the typography bug
Android real-device manual video Readability looks acceptable on recorded default-size screens

Evidence Review

The real-device video shows the login screen, app drawer, Real Estate tour list, Settings, and create-tour entry screens. Typography is generally readable and no obvious default-size clipping was observed in the recorded frames. However, this does not satisfy the full issue acceptance because source review shows OpenSans is not registered/rendered and hardcoded font sizes still remain in widgets.

Final QA Decision

Issue #1 should remain open as a bug. The visual default-device recording is acceptable, but the implementation does not meet the required OpenSans registration and single-source typography acceptance criteria. Marking this task with bug and Sanity Testing is appropriate; do not add unit testing for this failed result.

[Main] Update UI — Flutter Migration

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: The RN Main / Home screen is the project-list / dashboard entry point (src/pages/main, src/pages/home — see docs/analyze.md §3.2). It is the first screen after Init (see Rooter) and lists the user's local tour projects with their upload/sync status.

Goal

Build the Main screen UI in Flutter to match (and modernize) the RN app's project dashboard, using the new typography system and component conventions.

Scope

  • Recreate the Main/Home layout: project list, per-project status (draft / uploaded / published), and primary actions (open, create new tour).
  • Use the centralized typography scale (see [UI] Update Font Size) and a reusable widget structure (cards/list items, navbar, sidebar).
  • Wire the list to the local DB layer (see [App] Setup Local DB) so projects render from local data.
  • Empty state + loading state for the project list.

Out of Scope

  • Project Detail / capture / connection editing screens (separate migration tasks).
  • Backend upload flow (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Main screen renders the list of local tour projects from the local DB.
  • Each item shows name, address, and sync/upload status indicator.
  • Primary actions present: create new tour, open existing project.
  • Loading and empty states implemented.
  • Layout responsive across phone sizes; visual parity with the RN Main screen.
  • Uses shared typography + components (no one-off styles).

Grounded in docs/analyze.md §2 (capabilities), §3.2 (structure), and §6 (consistency recommendations).

[App] Setup Local DB — Flutter Migration

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: The RN app is offline-first and stores all tour data locally in SQLite (WAL mode), defined and migrated in src/pages/init.js. The Flutter app must replicate this local persistence layer. See docs/analyze.md §3.3 for the full data model.

Goal

Set up the local SQLite database in the Flutter app (e.g. sqflite / drift), recreating the existing schema and a clean migration mechanism, as the foundation for offline tour authoring.

Schema to replicate (from docs/analyze.md §3.3)

  • projects — id, project_name, address, user_id, project_type, uploaded, googleUploaded, isAutoConnect, virtual_tour_status, listing, attr, timestamps.
  • panoramas — id, panorama_original/thumbnail/small/tiny, latlng, heading, fov, width/height, level_id, project_id, uploaded, pano_id, stitching_id.
  • connections — id, main_id, link_id, meters, angle, draft, auto_connect_error, project_id.
  • levels — id, level_name, level_type, position, folder_id, project_id.

Scope

  • Initialize the DB on app start (equivalent of RN Init bootstrap) and create the 4 tables.
  • Implement a versioned migration system (improving on the RN PRAGMA table_info hand-rolled approach — see analysis §5/§6) so schema changes are tracked by version.
  • Provide a data-access layer (DAO/repository) with typed models for each table.
  • Enable WAL mode for concurrency parity.

Out of Scope

  • Cloud sync / upload to GoThru APIs (separate task).
  • Filesystem panorama image storage (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • DB initializes on first launch; the 4 tables (projects, panoramas, connections, levels) are created.
  • Versioned migration runner in place (no ad-hoc column-existence checks).
  • Typed Dart models + DAO/repository for CRUD on each table.
  • Basic round-trip verified: insert → query → update → delete a project and related panoramas/connections.
  • WAL mode enabled; offline read/write works with no network.

Directly addresses docs/analyze.md §3.3 (data model) and the migration-robustness recommendations in §5/§6.

Verdict: PASS
